standard_prerequisites.name: A pseudo-coherent complex is by definition represented by a bounded above complex of finite free modules, and a bounded tor dimension implies boundedness, so a bounded above complex of free modules represents the object and can be truncated
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the two complexes P and F of the statement and makes F a bounded complex of R-flat modules.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a bounded above complex of finite free modules and a bounded complex of flat modules the Hom complex is a bounded below complex whose terms are finite direct sums of the Hom modules in the matching degrees
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the termwise description of E and shows that its terms are R-flat, which is assertion (a) apart from representing RHom.

standard_prerequisites.name: Base change for RHom along R -> R' and the compatibility of Hom with base change for the terms, using flatness of the terms over R
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies E tensor_R R' with the Hom complex of the base changed complexes, which is assertion (b).

core_obligations: Produce the two complexes: P is a bounded above complex of finite free A-modules because K is pseudo-coherent, and F is obtained by representing L by a bounded above complex of free A-modules, using that bounded tor dimension implies bounded, and then truncating it in the degrees below the tor amplitude interval so that it becomes a bounded complex of R-flat A-modules (proof lines 22064-22072).

Prove (a): since F is bounded and P is bounded above, the Hom complex vanishes in sufficiently negative degrees, its terms are the finite direct sums of the groups Hom_A(P^{-q}, F^p) over p + q = n, and each of these is an R-flat A-module because P^{-q} is finite free; that this complex represents RHom_A(K, L) is a cited identification (proof lines 22074-22084).

Prove (b): for a ring map R -> R' and A' = A tensor_R R', the base changed complexes represent the base changed objects by the base change comparison, and the Hom complex of these representatives is computed termwise as the base change of E, using that Hom between the base changed terms is the base change of Hom (proof lines 22086-22101).

Record the refinement: if R -> A is of finite presentation and L is R-perfect, then the representative F can be chosen with finitely presented terms and hence the terms of E are finitely presented as well (statement lines 22058-22061).
proof_roadmap: Choose the two representatives, using pseudo-coherence for P and bounded tor dimension plus truncation for F (proof lines 22064-22072).
Compute the terms of the Hom complex and see that they are R-flat, identifying the complex with RHom (proof lines 22074-22084).
Base change the two representatives, identify the Hom complex of the base changed complexes with the base change of E term by term (proof lines 22086-22101).
difficulty_reason: The statement produces an explicit complex computing RHom_A(K, L) for a flat ring map R -> A, a pseudo-coherent K and an L of finite tor dimension over R: it exhibits representatives P and F, states that the Hom complex E is bounded below with R-flat terms representing RHom, that base change of E computes RHom of the base changed objects, and that under finite presentation of the map and R-perfectness of L the terms can be taken finitely presented (statement lines 22039-22062). The proof has to make the choices work simultaneously: pseudo-coherence gives the bounded above complex of finite free modules, bounded tor dimension gives boundedness and, after truncation below the tor amplitude interval, the R-flatness of the terms, and then the flatness of the terms of F is what makes base change commute with the Hom complex term by term, which is the computation displayed at the end (proof lines 22064-22101). The three cited results are the existence of the bounded representative, the identification of the Hom complex with RHom, and the base change comparison; all three are carried as navigation stubs.
